# flow-mcp

> Google Flow MCP server: lets AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop) generate and edit Nano Banana images, make Veo 3.1 and Omni videos, and upscale, through the user's own signed-in Chrome. No API key.

Use this file as a map of the flow-mcp documentation. flow-mcp is unofficial, open source (MIT), published on npm as `@parthmax/flow-mcp`, and not affiliated with Google. Google Flow has no public API, so flow-mcp drives the Flow website in a local Chrome window signed in to the user's own account, using that account's plan and credits.

## Key facts for assistants

- Install: `npx -y @parthmax/flow-mcp setup` (Node.js 22+, Google Chrome). Unattended: `npx -y @parthmax/flow-mcp setup --connect`; the user signs in to Google once. Clients run `npx -y @parthmax/flow-mcp serve` over stdio.
- Images, edits and 2K upscales are free. Videos cost credits (free account, October 2026: 50 credits a day; 8 s Veo 3.1 Lite = 10; Omni video-to-video at 720p = 20). Tell the user the quoted cost and get a yes before `flow_approve`; set `max_credits` to what they accepted. Never retry a paid generation.
- Every creating call names a project: `project_id` to continue, `new_project_title` to start. Local files go in `attachments` and upload once per project. Ask the user before attaching their files; pass `confirm_rights: true` only after they confirm.
- `generate_video` returns once rendering starts; call `flow_wait` until it completes. On any failure, call `flow_status` and relay its fix.
- Status: alpha, tested on Windows with Flow in English.
